parts.name: beam body

physics.Basic_description: The main long rectangular bar of the caliper, appearing silver with a matte metallic finish.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the rigid backbone and reference scale for measurements.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the flat sides or top/bottom surfaces of the beam away from the slider.
physics.reason: Caliper beams are solid machined metal bars to ensure rigidity and prevent flexing during measurement.

parts.description: The main long rectangular bar of the caliper, appearing silver with a matte metallic finish.
parts.function: Provides the rigid backbone and reference scale for measurements.

parts.name: beam scale

physics.Basic_description: The graduated markings etched into the top surface of the beam, appearing as dark lines on silver.
physics.Functional_description: Allows reading of the main measurement units (inches or mm).
physics.Grasped_description: Not a grasp target; part of the beam surface.
physics.reason: Etched surface feature of the solid metal beam.

parts.description: The graduated markings etched into the top surface of the beam, appearing as dark lines on silver.
parts.function: Allows reading of the main measurement units (inches or mm).

parts.name: beam web

physics.Basic_description: The central recessed channel or web running along the beam where the rack gear might be located.
physics.Functional_description: Structural reinforcement and housing for the rack mechanism.
physics.reason: Part of the solid machined beam structure.

parts.description: The central recessed channel or web running along the beam where the rack gear might be located.
parts.function: Structural reinforcement and housing for the rack mechanism.

parts.name: guide rail mark

physics.Basic_description: A thin strip or edge detail along the beam, likely a guide rail or reference edge.
physics.Functional_description: Guides the slider movement along the beam.
physics.reason: Integral part of the solid metal beam.

parts.description: A thin strip or edge detail along the beam, likely a guide rail or reference edge.
parts.function: Guides the slider movement along the beam.

parts.name: fixed jaw

physics.Basic_description: The stationary jaw at the left end of the beam, L-shaped and silver metallic.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the fixed reference point for external and internal measurements.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped by the vertical or horizontal section, though usually the beam is preferred.
physics.reason: Jaws are solid forged or machined metal to withstand clamping forces.

parts.description: The stationary jaw at the left end of the beam, L-shaped and silver metallic.
parts.function: Provides the fixed reference point for external and internal measurements.

parts.name: slider body

physics.Basic_description: The moving carriage that holds the dial and sliding jaw, silver metallic block.
physics.Functional_description: Slides along the beam to adjust the jaw opening and drive the dial mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the thumb roller area or the body of the slider to move it.
physics.reason: Slider bodies are often cast or machined shells with internal cavities for the gear mechanism and weight reduction, though thick-walled.

parts.description: The moving carriage that holds the dial and sliding jaw, silver metallic block.
parts.function: Slides along the beam to adjust the jaw opening and drive the dial mechanism.

parts.name: dial bezel

physics.Basic_description: The circular ring surrounding the dial face, shiny silver metal.
physics.Functional_description: Holds the dial glass in place and protects the mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be gripped by the rim to rotate the bezel for zeroing.
physics.reason: Bezel is a thin stamped or machined ring.

parts.description: The circular ring surrounding the dial face, shiny silver metal.
parts.function: Holds the dial glass in place and protects the mechanism.

parts.name: dial face

physics.Basic_description: The white circular background of the dial with black markings.
physics.Functional_description: Displays the fine measurement readings via the needle.
physics.reason: Likely a thin solid plastic or paper disc under glass.

parts.description: The white circular background of the dial with black markings.
parts.function: Displays the fine measurement readings via the needle.

parts.name: dial ticks

physics.Basic_description: The black graduation marks printed on the dial face.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a physical part to grasp.
physics.reason: Surface print/feature on the dial face.

parts.description: The black graduation marks printed on the dial face.

parts.name: lock screw boss

physics.Basic_description: The raised threaded housing on the slider where the lock screw sits.
physics.Functional_description: Provides threads for the locking screw to secure the slider.
physics.reason: Machined protrusion from the solid/cast slider body.

parts.description: The raised threaded housing on the slider where the lock screw sits.
parts.function: Provides threads for the locking screw to secure the slider.

parts.name: depth rod

physics.Basic_description: The thin metal rod extending from the right end of the beam.
physics.Functional_description: Used for measuring the depth of holes or steps.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be pinched gently, but fragile.
physics.reason: Depth rods are solid thin metal strips.

parts.description: The thin metal rod extending from the right end of the beam.
parts.function: Used for measuring the depth of holes or steps.

parts.name: needle

physics.Basic_description: The thin pointer inside the dial, likely black or red.
physics.Functional_description: Points to the current reading on the dial face.
physics.reason: Thin solid metal stamping.

parts.description: The thin pointer inside the dial, likely black or red.
parts.function: Points to the current reading on the dial face.

parts.name: lock screw head

physics.Basic_description: The small knurled screw head on top of the slider.
physics.Functional_description: Tightened to lock the slider in position.
physics.Grasped_description: Pinch and rotate to tighten or loosen.
physics.reason: Small machined solid screw.

parts.description: The small knurled screw head on top of the slider.
parts.function: Tightened to lock the slider in position.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
